Manufacturing Controls & HMI Standardization

Standardize operator interfaces and bring equipment state into useful production displays.

Manufacturing Controls Engineering Intern

01 Problem02 Requirements03 Concepts04 Engineering Analysis05 Design06 Build / Test07 Results08 What I Learned
01

Problem

During my controls engineering internship in Paints & Coatings in Austin, I worked on the interfaces and logic operators use to understand production equipment.

The work combined HMI standardization, Structured Text data extraction, and hardware/network integration.

02

Requirements

RequirementEngineering definition
ConsistencyStandardize HMI behavior across 15 PLCs supporting 130+ HMIs.
VisibilityImprove operator fault visibility and equipment-position displays.
DataExpose internal crane coordinate information in the HMI.
IntegrationSupport HMI installation and Profinet network connections.
03

Concepts

ITERATION / 01

Common interface conventions

Apply consistent display and fault information across the HMI installation.

ITERATION / 02

Useful equipment data

Extract crane coordinate data and map it into a display operators can use.

04

Engineering Analysis

I developed Structured Text logic to extract internal coordinate data for real-time crane-position viewing on the HMI.

HMI standardization required consistency across the PLCs and displays, while hardware work required attention to the configured network interfaces.

05

Design

I led HMI standardization across 15 PLCs supporting more than 130 HMIs, improving fault visibility for operators.

I also supported HMI hardware installations with technicians, including Profinet connections through Scalance and Cisco switches.

06

Build / Test

The internship work covered interface standardization, crane-position data mapping, and HMI hardware installation.

The scope was controls and production-system integration in Austin during Fall 2025.

07

Results

The work improved the consistency of operator-facing information and enabled real-time crane-position visibility, with reported savings exceeding $50,000.

15PLCs in the standardization scope
130+HMIs supported
$50k+reported cost savings
08

What I Learned

A control system needs to be understandable at the point of use. Consistent interfaces and clear equipment state help turn the underlying logic into something useful for operators.
